four_layer_diagnosis.biological_reference: partial -- the underlying commitment is that channel authority in an evaluator should be decided by CONTENT rather than by the accident of each channel's units, which is a real property of biological value integration (heterogeneous afferents are gain-normalised before they compete). The operator is a faithful translation of that idea. What is unexamined -- here and upstream -- is whether divisive normalisation to equal cross-candidate SD is the RIGHT normalisation, or merely A normalisation: equal-variance is a strong and unargued commitment about what 'commensurable' should mean.

biological_reference.closest_mechanism: Divisive normalisation / gain control at a value-integration stage, so that heterogeneous afferent channels compete on content rather than on the accident of their units (the canonical normalisation-model family; the same motivation the operator's own design doc gives).

a downstream stage that preserves the re-weighting rather than undoing it
channels that are live enough to be worth normalising

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: [2026-09-14, V3-EXQ-1012a, PASS, diagnostic] The acceptance instrument for SD-E3-CHANNEL-COMMENSURABILITY's AMENDED readiness target (GFLAG-0234, /governance option A, user-approved 2026-09-10), superseding the parked V3-EXQ-1012 whose original share-based target was found to be an arithmetic identity of the operator it was meant to validate. NOT a test of MECH-439 -- non_contributory, and the driver's own outcome_note says so: 'MECH-439's direction does not move on this record.' WHAT IT ESTABLISHES: the operator is not a no-op at the primary-score selection stage. Shadow OFF/ON replay, intra-tick with the EMA state frozen and a self-check replay that must reproduce the live scores exactly (0 failures in 8 of 8 cells), gives a primary-argmin flip rate of 0.821 fed / 0.724 starved over 158-258 genuine fresh selections per cell. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and what a reader must not infer: that the flip is principled. There is no null arm. The criterion's bar is computed from the same four seeds it tests (bar = 2 x sd of the arm's own rates, so it is a coefficient-of-variation test, not a test against any reference), and a differential rescaling that spans four orders of magnitude between the live channels would be expected to move the argmin at roughly the rate two unrelated rankings disagree -- so this run cannot distinguish 'the operator imposes a different, principled ranking' from 'the operator scrambles the ranking'. The reference it needs is a PLACEBO differential rescaling carrying no commensurability content. Two further scope bounds: the DV characterises the primary-score stage only, and the `final_commit_by_primary_frac` readout the driver's own docstring calls mandatory interpretive context was not emitted, so nothing relates these flips to the executed action; and two of the five declared commensurability channels (benefit_weighted, goal_weighted) have a scale estimate of exactly 0.0 in every cell, so the operator arbitrated among 3 live channels, not 5.

learning_extracted: THE RE-DERIVE BRAKE FIRES ON MECH-439 AT 15 HITS AGAINST A THRESHOLD OF 2 -- the dominant governance fact about this claim, and it is worth stating plainly because 15 is not 'a couple over the line'. The counted slugs span 2026-06-19 to 2026-09-02 and cover the 689/700/709/711/713 learned-gating and cross-loop-arbitration lineage, the 936/936a f-variance-share lineage, and the 571b/571c monopoly-presence lineage. What that record says is that MECH-439 has been approached from many directions and has never once been tested under conditions where it could express itself; every reading is a ceiling or a non-contributory instrument finding. The correct response is the one the brake mandates and this autopsy independently reached: build the upstream substrate, and refuse another lettered test of the claim.

THE VERDICT CRITERION IS EFFECTIVELY UNFAILABLE, AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS AUTOPSY UNDERSTATED IT (Step 7c red-team F2). The draft described `flip_rate_lift` as `mean_rate > 2 * sd`, a coefficient-of-variation test. The driver's actual predicate is weaker in two compounding ways: `bar = max(FLIP_RATE_SD_MULTIPLIER * sd, FLIP_RATE_ABS_FLOOR)` with the floor at 0.01, and then `passed = mean_clears_bar OR majority_clears_floor`, where `majority_clears_floor` is true when at least half the seeds have a flip rate above 0.01. Any arm in which half the seeds flip the argmin more than 1% of the time passes on the second disjunct alone, whatever the first says -- and the manifest's own `criteria[0].detail` records `majority_clears_floor: True` for both arms. FURTHER: every CONTENT branch of the verdict ladder emits PASS, including `operator_selection_inconsequential_primary_stage`; the only FAIL branches are instrument-defect, arm-gate-red, and the hidden-identity flag. So `outcome: PASS` carries no information about the direction of the measurement at all. Recorded as a correction to this artifact's own first draft, not only to the driver: reading a criterion's REPORTED cells is not reading its PREDICATE, and the two differed here.

THE SD USED IS THE POPULATION SD, NOT THE SAMPLE SD, AND WITH n=4 THAT MATTERS ARITHMETICALLY THOUGH NOT HERE. Reported fed sd 0.10687 is pstdev over the 4 rates (sample stdev is 0.12340); starved 0.24013 is pstdev (sample 0.27727). Since pstdev under-estimates by sqrt(3/4) = 0.866 at n=4, the bar is ~13% lower than a sample-sd bar would be. Recomputed both ways: fed 0.8214 clears 0.2137 and 0.2468; starved 0.7242 clears 0.4803 and 0.5545. Neither verdict flips, so this is hygiene rather than a finding -- recorded so a later recompute does not read as a discrepancy, and so the successor picks the convention deliberately.

THE FLIP RATE HAS NO REFERENCE VALUE -- and the first draft's ARGUMENT for that was wrong in a way worth recording (Step 7c red-team F4). THE CONCLUSION STANDS: 0.8214 fed / 0.7242 starved is uninterpretable without a null, because nothing in the run says what an uninformative differential rescaling would produce. THE DRAFT'S REASONING DID NOT: it argued that OFF and ON rankings are computed over 'effectively disjoint information' (OFF decided by residue alone, ON by an equalised 3-way sum) and therefore agree at chance, ~1/k, making 0.82 unremarkable. That premise is false -- the ON score RETAINS residue, at roughly 1/3 weight rather than at monopoly weight, so the two rankings are correlated, not independent. The red-team's Monte Carlo under genuine independence at k=8 gives ~0.63, and the OBSERVED 0.82 EXCEEDS it. So if anything the observed flip rate is higher than an independence baseline would predict, which is mildly favourable to the operator rather than damning. The honest statement is the narrow one: there is no measured null, so the number cannot be graded -- not that the number is at chance. The draft's framing was directionally misleading and is withdrawn rather than quietly edited.

WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED: THE PERMUTATION PLACEBO THIS AUTOPSY FIRST PROPOSED IS A STRAW NULL, SATISFIED BY CONSTRUCTION (Step 7c red-team F1). The first draft recommended, as the missing reference arm, a permutation of the fitted per-channel scales across channels -- argmin-affecting, magnitude-matched, information-free. The magnitude-matching is exactly what breaks it. From this run's own fed seed-42 scales (f_weighted 6.63e-05, harm_weighted 2.57e-03, residue_weighted 0.675), a permutation does not EQUALISE the channels; it installs a NEW monopoly. 4 of the 5 non-identity permutations leave residue_weighted the monopolist by ratios from 6.8 to 4e5 -- i.e. they reproduce the OFF ranking, so the placebo's flip rate would be near zero -- and the fifth crowns harm at 39:1. None equalises. So 'operator flip rate > placebo flip rate' could not have failed: the autopsy would have shipped, as its repair, THE SAME DEFECT CLASS the tautology doc found in the target it was repairing. Recorded rather than silently swapped, because the near-miss is the lesson: a null must be checked against the run's OWN measured scales before it is recommended, not argued for in the abstract. The replacements are in routing_detail.required_changes and neither has this property -- the prior tautology doc's own option (2), which needs no new arm at all, and a tick-shuffled scale estimator, which preserves per-channel equalisation while destroying tick-local content.

`evidence_direction: "diagnostic"` IS NOT MERELY A DEAD LETTER -- IT IS CURRENTLY SCORING THIS RUN AS `supports` FOR MECH-439 IN THE LIVE INDEX (Step 7c red-team F3; the first draft got the mechanism half right and the consequence badly wrong). The chain, every link verified in source and in the landed index: (i) `build_experiment_indexes._normalize_direction` allows exactly {supports, weakens, mixed, unknown, superseded, non_contributory, inconclusive, does_not_support} and returns `unknown` for anything else, so 'diagnostic' becomes `unknown` -- that much the draft had. (ii) `direction_explicitly_set` is computed as `bool(manifest.get('evidence_direction_note'))`, and THIS MANIFEST CARRIES NO `evidence_direction_note` (nor an `evidence_direction_per_claim`), so the flag is False. (iii) The indexer then RE-INFERS: `if inferred_direction == 'unknown' and not run.direction_explicitly_set: inferred_direction = 'supports' if run.final_status == 'PASS' else 'weakens'`. The run is a PASS. (iv) The result is live in `evidence/experiments/claim_evidence.v1.json` RIGHT NOW: claim_id MECH-439, `evidence_direction: "supports"`, `confidence: 0.75`, `confidence_rationale: "PASS with supporting direction"`, `adjudication: "verified"`. The ONLY thing preventing that from reaching MECH-439's posterior is `scoring_excluded: "diagnostic_probe"`. So a run whose own driver says in its outcome_note that 'MECH-439's direction does not move on this record' is recorded in the index as verified supporting evidence for MECH-439, on a claim that is simultaneously under a fired re-derive brake at 15 ceiling hits. THE FIX IS CHEAP AND MUST BE BOTH HALVES: emit `evidence_direction: non_contributory` (in the allowed set, so no normalisation loss) AND emit an `evidence_direction_note` (which sets `direction_explicitly_set` and blocks the re-inference outright). Either alone helps; only both close it. This is the same failure family as the `claim_directions` dead letter the confirmed failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-1004_2026-09-05 found one lineage over, and it is worse, because this one does not merely fail to record an intent -- it records the opposite of it.

THE TWO DEAD CHANNELS ARE DEAD BECAUSE THEIR BRANCHES WERE NEVER ENTERED, NOT BECAUSE A COMPUTED CHANNEL HAD ZERO SPREAD (Step 7c red-team F5 -- a sharpening of the draft's own finding). `benefit_weighted` and `goal_weighted` carry a scale estimate of exactly 0.0 in all 8 cells. The draft read that as 'those channels have no cross-candidate spread on any tick', which is true but misleading: the benefit branch is never fed by this driver's warmup at all, and the goal branch is never active -- the manifest's own `z_goal_stream` reads `ticks_active: 0` and `active_frac: 0.0` against `writer_calls: 53837`. So they are not low-variance channels, they are absent ones. The substrate handles it correctly either way -- `_commensurability_scale` returns the 1.0 no-op for any channel at or below `e3_commensurability_floor`, explicitly because 'a structurally-dead channel divided by its own near-zero spread would otherwise explode', so there is no blow-up. The scope consequence is unchanged and stands: the operator arbitrated among 3 live channels, not the 5 it declares. The cause matters for the successor, though -- reviving those channels is a HARNESS change, not a tuning one.

THE DRIVER'S DOCSTRING PROMISES A READOUT THE BUILD DOES NOT EMIT, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT BOUNDS THE DV'S REACH. The docstring states that `final_commit_by_primary_frac` 'is recorded per cell (matching the parked driver's own C6 diagnostic) as mandatory interpretive context', and explains exactly why it matters: on a cell where it is low, a primary-stage flip rate does not tell you whether the operator changed the EXECUTED action. It is absent from `arm_results` (whose 26 keys are listed in the artifact facts section), and both `outcome_note` and `custom_information.build_scoping_decision` say it was deliberately not carried in this build. So the build scoping decision is honestly recorded in two places and the DOCSTRING is stale relative to it. The consequence is real: this run measures flips at the primary-score stage and nothing relates them to the action the agent took. A reader who trusts the docstring will believe the bound exists.

`evidence_direction: "diagnostic"` IS A DEAD LETTER -- it silently becomes `unknown`. `build_experiment_indexes._normalize_direction` allows exactly {supports, weakens, mixed, unknown, superseded, non_contributory, inconclusive, does_not_support} and returns `unknown` for anything else. 'diagnostic' is not in that set, so the driver's evident intent -- mark this as a run that should not score its claim -- reaches the index as `unknown`, which is ALSO the value a manifest gets for simply omitting the field. The intent is therefore indistinguishable from an omission, and `unknown` is not inert downstream (it is one of the values the indexer's fail-hit branch treats as scoreable context). This is the same class of defect the confirmed failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-1004_2026-09-05 found in the `claim_directions` field, one lineage over: the mechanically honest emission for a run that is not scoring its claim is `non_contributory`, not a word describing the run's purpose. Cheap confirmer: read `_normalize_direction`'s `allowed` set.

`regimes_differ: true` IS A NON-FORCED-NESS FLAG AND ITS NAME OVERSELLS IT. The driver is precise about this in its own prose -- the check exists so that a DV reading identically in both regimes would be caught as evidence of a hidden identity -- and the floor is set accordingly at 0.02. But the manifest field is named `regimes_differ` and reads `true` on a gap of |0.8214 - 0.7242| = 0.0972 against per-seed sds of 0.107 and 0.240, which is deep inside noise. Nothing in this autopsy turns on it, and the driver did not overclaim; the successor should rename the emitted field to match the prose (`regime_difference_above_forcedness_floor`) so a governance reader cannot take it for a statistical difference.

WHAT THIS DRIVER GOT RIGHT, recorded because it is the standard the rest of the batch should be read against. Recording is COMPLETE -- the only one of the three manifests in this staging batch with no always-core gap (config, seeds, elapsed_seconds 7381.9s, substrate_hash, substrate_commit clean, substrate_identity, arm_fingerprint per cell). The shadow comparison is INTRA-TICK on captured calls with the EMA state frozen, so the counterfactual is genuinely same-tick and same-candidate-set. The SELF-CHECK replay at the live config value must reproduce the live scores exactly or the driver refuses to report -- it found 10/10 failures in its own pre-fix smoke and 0/8 here, which is a working instrument-correctness gate rather than a decorative one. Readiness is asserted per arm with four named preconditions including `clamp_config_landed` and `residue_protocol_landed`, both of which guard against the silent-kwargs class of failure. And the regime manipulation demonstrably landed: residue_weighted scale 0.48-6.03 fed against 9.3e-05-6.9e-04 starved.

A COUNTING-CONVENTION INCONSISTENCY IN THE RE-DERIVE BRAKE, SURFACED FOR GOVERNANCE AND NOT FIXED HERE (Step 7c red-team F6). This autopsy excludes itself from MECH-439's ceiling count on the grounds that it is a substrate ACCEPTANCE INSTRUMENT rather than a ceiling reading, and stamps `standard` per-claim so the counter's short-circuit drops it. But two of the 15 hits it cites -- failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-571b_2026-09-01 and failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-571c_2026-09-02 -- are the SAME epistemic shape (instrument/measurement findings about the monopoly and about the operator's own readiness target) and they DO count under the same recipe.
